identity.name: United Arab Republic
alt_names: Egypt as the United Arab Republic (1961-1971)

land.text: Egypt, the Egyptian region of the union

predecessors.note: The union was announced on 1 February 1958 and formed on 22 February 1958 (UAR page).

land.text: Syria, the Northern region of the union

predecessors.note: Kuwatli and Nasser announced the merger on 1 February 1958; Syria remained in the UAR until 28 September 1961.

land.text: Egypt less the Israeli-occupied Sinai; the name 'Arab Republic of Egypt' was adopted in September 1971

successors.note: Cliopatria's Arab Republic of Egypt row begins in 1973, so 1972 has no row; the same state carries on under the new name from September 1971.

land.text: Syria, seceded on 28 September 1961 after a coup

successors.note: A mid-life hand-over, not the UAR's end: Egypt kept the name United Arab Republic until 1971.

capitals.name: Cairo
capitals.note: Infobox: 'Capital and largest city: Cairo'; the page adds that Damascus also served as a seat of central authority.

rulers.name: Anwar Sadat
rulers.title: President (acting from 28 September 1970)
rulers.note: Acting from 28 September 1970 to 15 October 1970, then president to 11 September 1971; the infobox also lists Mahmoud Fawzi as '1970-1971 (last)', which the page's table does not.

keyframe_review.note: 1958-1959, 1.199 M km2 against the infobox's 1,195,000 km2 (no year given; ratio 1.00): Egypt with Sinai and Syria, the two regions of the union ('Egypt and Gaza (Egyptian-governed), and Syria until 1961'). Cliopatria starts in 1958 as the union does (formed 22 February). The shape also takes in the three Gaza cells and the Halaib Triangle, which the ledger treats as an administered strip (from 1959) and a disputed zone (February 1958).

correction.text: Egypt and Syria, the union as it stood to the coup of 28 September 1961 ('Syrian independence restored'); holds 1960-1961 only, not to 1966; Gaza (Egyptian-administered, not annexed) is left to the occupation event

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria draws Syria inside the UAR to 1966, but the coup of 28 September 1961 gave 'Syrian independence restored' (infobox) and Egypt alone kept the name until 1971 (UAR page). The shape is right only for 1960 to September 1961 (Syria in), and Gaza is carried as Egyptian-administered land (occupation event from 1959). From 1962 see united-arab-republic_1962.

correction.text: Egypt alone, still called the United Arab Republic, with Sinai; Gaza administered but not annexed

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1962-1966, which Cliopatria draws with Syria still inside: 'After Syria left, Egypt's official name stayed United Arab Republic until 1971'. Egypt alone, with Sinai, less the Gaza Strip it administered. The cells left after subtracting Cliopatria's Syria shape and Gaza are the 1967 shape plus the Sinai Peninsula, so nothing else is cut.

1967-1968, 0.95 M km2: Egypt without the Sinai Peninsula, matching 'On 8 June, Israel completed the capture of the Sinai' (the 1967 shape is exactly Egypt's cells less Sinai). Israel's occupation is the ledger's occupation_start; check that the Israel dossier's 1967 shape does not also draw Sinai as solid Israeli land. No infobox figure for Egypt alone to compare. Reviewer me-10-k (2026-10-25): verdict ok changed to adjust. Occupied land is hatched in the occupier's colour over the owner's (master plan rule 4), and this batch keeps the owner's shape under an occupation elsewhere (state-of-kuwait 1990, Iraq cutting Kuwait out); Cliopatria's 1967 shape drops the Sinai altogether, which would leave the hatch over no owner. The correction is the 1962-1966 shape, Egypt with Sinai.

correction.text: Egypt with the Sinai Peninsula, less the Gaza Strip (the 1962-1966 keyframe's cells): the Sinai, occupied by Israel from June 1967, stays Egypt's land under the hatch of the ledger's occupation event
Egypt with the Sinai Peninsula, less the Gaza Strip: the Sinai stays Egypt's land under Israeli occupation (hatched by the ledger); holds 1969 to September 1971, then the Arab Republic of Egypt

keyframe_review.note: Same shape as 1967 (Egypt less Sinai). Cliopatria runs the row to 1972, but the page gives the renaming to 'Arab Republic of Egypt' as 2 September 1971 (text) or 11 September 1971 (infobox); the shape holds 1969-1971 and the successor carries it on. Unchanged as a shape; only the end year moves. Reviewer me-10-k (2026-10-25): correction changed from the unchanged Cliopatria shape to Egypt with the Sinai, as for 1967: the occupied Sinai is drawn as Egypt's land under the occupation hatch.

region.text: Egypt, with Cairo as capital, the first region of the union

ledger.note: 1958: Egypt and Syria unite as the United Arab Republic under Nasser. 'The United Arab Republic was established on 1 February 1958' (the announcement); referendums followed on 21 February, the result was announced on 22 February and Nasser was declared president; infobox formation 22 February 1958.

region.text: Syria as the Northern region of the union, until 1961

ledger.note: 1958: Syria joins the union as its Northern region. Infobox regions: 'Egypt and Gaza (Egyptian-governed), and Syria until 1961'; the navbox also lists a looser United Arab States of 1958-1961 with the Mutawakkilite Kingdom of Yemen, which is an association and not territory.

region.text: the disputed Halaib Triangle, 20,580 km2, between the 1899 line on the 22nd parallel and the 1902 administrative boundary

ledger.note: February 1958: Egypt sends troops into the Halaib Triangle. Sudan was planning elections there and 'Nasser sent troops into the disputed region' for the referendum on union with Syria.

February 1958: Egypt withdraws its troops from the Halaib Triangle 'the same month'. The dispute stayed open (the area took part in Sudanese elections until the late 1980s and 'joint control remained in effect until 1992'), so Cliopatria's inclusion of the triangle in the UAR shape is a claim, not control.

region.text: the Gaza Strip under Egyptian administration

ledger.note: 1959: Egyptian administration of the Gaza Strip. 'Egyptian administration of Gaza: 1959' (infobox); after the All-Palestine Government was dissolved in 1959 the UAR 'further exerted administration over Gaza, until 1967'. Administered, never annexed, hence the hatch rather than the solid colour.

28 September 1961: a coup in Damascus ends the union. The infobox lists 'Syrian independence restored' and by the night of 28 September 'it was clear that they had chosen independence'; Jordan and Turkey recognised the new regime on 29 September, Nasser recognised 'the fact of Syrian secession' on 5 October, and 870 Egyptian officers and soldiers were sent home on 2 November after under 200 paratroopers landed at Latakia and were surrounded.

region.text: the Gaza Strip, taken with Gaza City on 6 June

ledger.note: 6 June 1967: Egyptian administration of Gaza ends. Israeli forces 'took Gaza City along with the entire Strip' on 6 June.

region.text: the Sinai Peninsula, up to the Suez Canal

ledger.note: June 1967: Israel occupies the Sinai Peninsula. 'On 8 June, Israel completed the capture of the Sinai'; Arish fell on 6 June and Sharm el-Sheikh on 7 June; Egypt accepted a cease-fire on 8 June. The occupation outlasts this dossier (the UAR page: 'Egypt recovered partial sovereignty over the Sinai Peninsula in 1978') and its occupation_end belongs to the Arab Republic of Egypt.

September 1971: Egypt becomes the Arab Republic of Egypt. The text says it 'formally changed its name to the Arab Republic of Egypt on 2 September 1971', the infobox says 11 September 1971; the referendums on the Federation of Arab Republics (Egypt, Libya, Syria) were held on 1 September 1971 and the federation, an association with no territory of its own, took effect on 1 January 1972. Same state, same land: a name change, handed to the Arab Republic of Egypt row.

wars.name: Six-Day War

zones.text: Gaza City and the entire Strip, 6 June

wars.outcome: Israeli victory, 5-10 June 1967: Israel occupied the Sinai and the Gaza Strip (from Egypt), the West Bank (from Jordan) and the Golan Heights (from Syria), 'a total of 70,000 km2'; Egypt and Jordan accepted a cease-fire on 8 June, Syria on 9 June, signed with Israel on 11 June.
wars.note: The Syrian front (Golan) is recorded in the Syrian dossiers; the page gives no km2 for any single area.

wars.name: Halaib crisis of 1958
wars.outcome: Egyptian troops entered the triangle in February 1958 and withdrew the same month; the sovereignty dispute continued, with Sudan holding or sharing the area until Egypt moved in during 1994-1995.
wars.note: A crisis, not a war: no shots are recorded on the page.

wars.name: 1961 Syrian coup d'état and secession
wars.outcome: Syria left the union on 28 September 1961; Nasser called off a landing at Latakia and recognised the secession on 5 October. No territory was fought over; the border moved by the secession alone.

certainty.note: Egyptian and Syrian frontiers follow treaty and armistice lines; the exceptions are the Halaib Triangle (disputed with Sudan) and the Gaza Strip (administered under the 1949 armistice, not annexed).

The Sinai front is a cease-fire line along the Suez Canal after June 1967 (the page says Israeli forces reached 'various points along the length of the Suez Canal'), so that edge is only as sharp as the line held; the Halaib Triangle stays disputed.

notes: Written by me-10-k on 2026-10-25 from five pages. (1) Cliopatria's 1960-1966 row keeps Syria inside the UAR for five years after the 28 September 1961 secession; it also overlaps the Republic of Syria and Ba'athist Syria rows (1961-1966). Verdicts: 1960 shape adjust (holds to 1961), new keyframe 1962-1966 for Egypt alone. (2) The row ends in 1972 but Egypt took its present name in September 1971, and the Arab Republic of Egypt row starts in 1973: 1972 has no row, so the Arab Republic of Egypt dossier must start in September 1971 (or the gap-filler must extend this one). (3) The Sinai occupation begun in June 1967 runs past this dossier (the UAR page: 'Egypt recovered partial sovereignty over the Sinai Peninsula in 1978'); its occupation_end belongs to arab-republic-of-egypt, so the validator warns that occupation_start has no later end here. (4) Gaza 1959-1967 is an administration, recorded as occupation with the Cliopatria row 'Palestinians' (1948) as counterpart; the page dates the start only to 1959 and says nothing on Egyptian control of Gaza before that. (5) The United Arab States of 1958-1961 (Egypt, Syria, Kingdom of Yemen) and the Federation of Arab Republics (1972-1977) are associations and need umbrella dossiers, not territory. (6) Not opened (page budget): any page on Egypt's relations with Yemen after 1961 or on the Egypt-Libya border; the five pages opened record no border move there. (7) Gazetteer names needed: 'Halaib Triangle'. (8) The page's table gives Nasser to 28 September 1970; the infobox's Mahmoud Fawzi entry is unexplained.
